findings.title: A rigged STREAM entity can drain other entities' principal from the shared VanaPoolTreasury
findings.root_cause: Shares are minted via a truncated rate (totalShares*1e18/activeRewardPool) that an owner can steer, while a bonded position's cost basis is booked at raw msg.value; an early exit refunds that raw cost basis from the shared treasury but debits the entity only the smaller share value, so other entities' principal is drained.

findings.title: A malicious entity owner can capture or withhold the rewards the splitter has already paid to their entity's stakers
findings.root_cause: Splitter payouts only credit the STREAM entity's locked pool and reach stakers only when the owner installs a vesting schedule, at which point commission (up to 100%) is taken at the then-current rate, so the owner can withhold or capture rewards stakers already earned.

findings.title: A large matured position nullifies the bonding period for subsequent deposits
findings.root_cause: The new eligibility timestamp is currentTimestamp + stakeAmount*bondingPeriod/newTotalValue, so a large existing matured position shrinks the bond applied to new capital to almost nothing.

findings.title: Accrued commission can never be withdrawn from the treasury
findings.root_cause: claimCommission has VanaPoolEntity call the treasury's transferVana, which requires DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE that the entity contract does not hold, so commission withdrawals always revert.

findings.title: Redelegating into a matured position makes already earned rewards forfeitable
findings.root_cause: stake() banks a matured position's gain into vestedRewards and resets the cost basis before re-bonding, but redelegate into a matured position skips that step, so already-earned rewards become forfeitable again.

findings.title: Reward distribution weight can be increased by settling rewards early
findings.root_cause: The splitter weights entities by stake-seconds of activeRewardPool, and the permissionless processRewards moves value from the locked to the active pool, so anyone can inflate an entity's weight by settling early.

findings.title: Rounding dust left by the final unstake disables an entity
findings.root_cause: entityShareToVana guards the empty case on share supply but vanaToEntityShare guards on pool size, so floor-division dust left after the last holder exits makes the share rate 0 and new deposits mint nothing.

findings.title: The executeBuyAndBurn(...) function sends tokens to a configurable sink address instead of destroying them
findings.root_cause: The burn transfers pendingBurn to a configurable sink address rather than destroying it, so totalSupply never falls and the buy-and-burn feature does not work.

findings.title: The entity registration stake never serves a bonding period
findings.root_cause: registerEntityStake writes shares and cost basis but never sets rewardEligibilityTimestamp, so the owner's registration stake is unbonded from creation.
